findings.task: A valid registration succeeds and creates exactly one network user.
A newly-registered user is a member of the community site.
Registering the same email twice fails cleanly and creates no second account.
The pre-seeded existing persona's stored credentials authenticate.
Logging in with a username resolves the right network identity.
Logging in with a email address resolves the right network identity.
A network user who is not a community member cannot log into the community-facing app surface.
A moderator applying a ban should never trigger an uncaught fatal error just because the notification email could not be queued.

evidence.crash: Cannot use object of type WP_Error as array

findings.task: A refresh token only works on the device it was issued to, and rotates on each use.
Replaying a superseded (already-rotated) refresh token is detected and rejected.
Detecting a replay burns the entire refresh-token family, not just the reused token.
One authenticated user cannot log out a different user's device by guessing its device ID.
The real browser registration form actually created a network user.
extrachill_users_create_browser_handoff_token() is unavailable or the browser registration did not produce a user; cross-site continuity could not be exercised.

cases.task: A visitor can reach a real login/register page on the community site.
A newly-registered visitor can reach a real onboarding page on the community site.
An invalid registration attempt (invalid-email) is rejected and never mutates the network user count.
An invalid registration attempt (password-mismatch) is rejected and never mutates the network user count.
An invalid registration attempt (short-password) is rejected and never mutates the network user count.
An invalid registration attempt (invalid-device) is rejected and never mutates the network user count.
An invalid registration attempt (null-password) is rejected and never mutates the network user count.
An invalid registration attempt (oversized-email) is rejected and never mutates the network user count.
A valid registration succeeds and creates exactly one network user.
A newly-registered user is a member of the community site.
Registering the same email twice fails cleanly and creates no second account.
The pre-seeded existing persona's stored credentials authenticate.
Logging in with a username resolves the right network identity.
Logging in with a email address resolves the right network identity.
A bad password on an unknown identifier looks identical to a bad password on a real one, so an attacker cannot tell which accounts exist.
A network user who is not a community member cannot log into the community-facing app surface.
A moderated (banned) user cannot obtain a session, even with correct credentials.
A moderator applying a ban should never trigger an uncaught fatal error just because the notification email could not be queued.

cases.task: A logged-out visitor is refused by every authenticated-only route (me, logout, browser-handoff).
A browser-handoff request pointed at an unsafe destination (https://outside.example/escape) is rejected.
A browser-handoff request pointed at an unsafe destination (https://extrachill.com.outside.example/escape) is rejected.
A browser-handoff request pointed at an unsafe destination (https://extrachill.link/escape) is rejected.
A browser-handoff request pointed at an unsafe destination (//community.extrachill.com/relative) is rejected.
A browser-handoff request pointed at an unsafe destination (javascript:alert(1)) is rejected.
A refresh token only works on the device it was issued to, and rotates on each use.
Replaying a superseded (already-rotated) refresh token is detected and rejected.
Detecting a replay burns the entire refresh-token family, not just the reused token.
One authenticated user cannot log out a different user's device by guessing its device ID.
Reserved/invalid onboarding usernames are all rejected without mutating completion state.
A user completing onboarding while passing another user's ID cannot rename that other user.
Completing onboarding twice is rejected the second time.
A login redirect_to parameter can never send a user off the Extra Chill network.
Five bad-password attempts trip the real rate limiter, and the limit cannot be bypassed by logging in with the account's email instead of its username.
The real browser registration form actually created a network user.
